core.title: Import only from your own or a lower layer within a layered subsystem
core.given: a file inside a named layer of a layered subsystem tree (which trees form the subsystem, the layer ladder lowest to highest, and how a file's layer is derived from its path come from the profile)
core.when: any of its imports resolves into the same layered subsystem (the specifier forms that count as resolving into it come from the profile's internal-import idiom)
core.then: each such import MUST target the file's own layer or a lower one; an edge into a higher layer (an upward edge) is forbidden
prefer: Keep imports same-layer or downward, following the subsystem's declared layer order from lowest to highest.
Reuse an existing artifact from a lower layer when possible.
Move a genuinely shared piece only to the lowest layer that actually owns it.
Compose upward rather than importing upward.
avoid: Reshuffling unrelated files of the subsystem.
Creating a new layer or generic abstraction for one dependency.
Hiding an upward dependency behind an aggregator module.
unless: Imports within the same layer are allowed.
Files directly under the subsystem root, outside any named layer, are not layered.

Test files and vendored/build trees are never scanned; a file counts as a test file when it matches any of the profile's undifferentiated test-file name patterns (all test kinds together, not split by test kind).
No layered subsystem tree in the repository: not judged; there is no system to connect to yet.
core.why: A hierarchy is only a hierarchy if dependencies flow one way; a lower-layer piece that imports a higher-layer one cannot be reused without dragging it along, and the layers collapse into one tangle.
evidence: The current behavioral or rendering acceptance passes.
All affected imports of the subsystem follow the declared direction; the stack's dependency-direction check reports no upward edge.
verification: Resolve each import of a file in a named layer to its target layer within the subsystem, using the profile's internal-import specifier forms (both relative and aliased forms that resolve into the tree count), and flag any edge whose target layer is higher than the source layer; the finding is the evaluation output, not an activation precondition.
Every import of a scoped file is inspected, whether the import is new or pre-existing.
Same-layer edges pass; files directly under the subsystem root (no named layer) are not layered; a repository with no subsystem tree is not judged (self-scoping).

Test files are never scanned: the check skips any file matching the profile's undifferentiated test-file name patterns (one exclusion list covering all test files, not attributed to a particular test kind). Vendored/build trees are never scanned; their exact classification is deferred to the stack's single exclusion list, which that checker owns.
The profile's declared layer ranking is authoritative; where prose lists the layers as a linear chain of steps, the declared ranking wins (layers tied at one rank count as the same layer).
A realization's file-kind coverage limitation does not narrow the rule's applicability to other files of the layered subsystem.

values: file inside a layered subsystem tree
file assigned to a named layer of the subsystem
file contains an import that resolves into the same layered subsystem

fires: A file in one layer of the subsystem imports from a higher layer of the same subsystem, whether the import is new or pre-existing.
The upward import is written through an aliased specifier as well as through a relative path — both forms count.
A file in the subsystem's lowest layer(s) imports from any layer above them.
doesNotFire: The repository has no layered subsystem tree.
A file imports another file in its own layer.
A file imports from a lower layer (downward edge).
The importing file is a test file or lives in a vendored/build tree.
The file sits directly under the subsystem root, outside any named layer.

profileRequirements.meaning: The code trees to which this layer rule applies: the trees whose internal directories form the layered subsystem; a repository with none of them is not judged.
profileRequirements.bunValue: **/design/**, **/design_system/**, **/design-system/** — a directory named design, design_system or design-system is a design root

profileRequirements.meaning: The ranked layer names inside those trees, in dependency order lowest to highest with their local names; ties may share a rank, and layers tied at one rank count as the same layer.
profileRequirements.bunValue: tokens or foundations (0), primitives (1), components (2), templates (3)

profileRequirements.meaning: How a file inside such a tree is assigned its layer from its path, and that a file with no named layer is out of scope (not layered), not a violation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the first directory beneath the design root names the layer; files directly under the root, with no named layer, are not layered

profileRequirements.meaning: The undifferentiated name patterns that mark a file as a test file of any kind, used as a scan exclusion; the patterns are not attributed to a particular test kind.

neutralityNotes: Round-4 change per audit: the test-file exclusion no longer splits Bun's *.test.* / *.spec.* across suffix.unit_test and suffix.acceptance_test. It now rides on one proposed key, suffix.test, holding the undifferentiated test-file name patterns (Bun value: *.test.*, *.spec.*), so the exact exclusion union is preserved without assigning artifact-kind semantics the rewrite does not state. Otherwise unchanged: the subsystem trees ride on layout.code_trees, the ranked ladder on roles.layers (ties share a rank, tied layers count as one layer), and path-based layer assignment plus unlayered-file treatment on roles.assignment; the intra-subsystem import-resolution idiom (relative specifiers and aliases naming the tree) is profile data through the proposed idiom.module_boundaries#internal_import key. Kept in the Bun realization: the concrete alias example `@/design/components/Card`, the validator id bun_design_system_detector and finding id upward_import, the tokens/foundations tie-break wording (reduced to 'the profile's declared ranking is authoritative'), and the detector's .tsx/.jsx/.html/.css coverage limitation. Severity 3 and strict disposition stay in core:verification, as does the deference of vendored/build exclusions to the stack's single exclusion list.
